notes: Coverage: every text block, every inline formula and every displayed formula on scan 003 was compared against both supplied witnesses from the whole layout view and the two full-resolution halves. The quoted phrases, spelling, accents, hyphens, punctuation, indices, primes, alphabet forms, underlines, arrow directions and hand/type distinctions were checked. Wholly agreed expressions are recorded in notation/coverage, not as changes.

Workflow: the whole image was opened exactly once for layout, then half a and half b exactly once in that order. Thirteen tight crops were made from the original image and each was opened once. No OCR, PDF text layer, web research, other scan image, other reader output or delegation was used. The notation snapshot was treated only as prior readings to test against this page.

The first recorded clock time follows the initial brief and packet read. Viewing timestamps are the tool clock reading immediately after the relevant image was displayed; crop groups were recorded after their last displayed crop.

The page is a typescript continuation with a pen page number 2 at the top and a lighter archive pencil 2 at lower-left. No title, date, salutation, signature, author-written total page count or other independent drawing appears on this scan. Pen additions are conservatively labelled another unnamed hand in the inventory; that label does not assert that different additions have different authors.

The opening paragraph identifies the auto-equivalences of A, the champ of right F-torsors, with bitorseurs and calls their tensor composition the Baer composition. It goes on to interpret the relevant bitorseurs as invertible bi-Modules when F has the displayed structure-sheaf unit form. These are statements on the page, not independently verified conclusions of this reading.

Under Structure the page associates pi_0(C), pi_1(C), and an action defined through the two Aut arrows. It explicitly says On prouve que pi_1(C) est un groupe commutatif and states the resulting module structure. The page then chooses L_a and phi_{a,b}, turns the associator into an automorphism of L_abc and writes f(a,b,c) in pi_1(C).

The lower paragraph states that a functorial associator is equivalent to the displayed three-variable application f. It uses On vérifie alors to state the equivalence of the pentagon axiom and a 3-cocycle condition, then says that a 2-cochaine change g modifies f to f+dg and gives a 3-cohomologie class. These authorial assertions were transcribed; no proof, independent re-proof, computation, certificate or mathematical consistency check was performed.

H records no editorial note quoting any of the deleted undertext on this scan. Its add/emph notation was compared by content and state, rather than counted merely for macro names. Its two-arrow notation agrees in content with the diagram; this was redrawn in the required tikzcd wrapper without inventing a content difference.

C doubt decisions: auto- underlying ot resolved; bitorseurs underlying t resolved; évidente remains uncertain with e placed first instead of s; the mark after un retained; Les/les retained; de 1 resolved; old à/a retained; cancelled two-unit fragment retained as doubtful; cancelled (du pen retained; second cochaine corrected undertext expanded to ah and the old letters read without doubt; initial p in correspondants resolved. A new uncertainty marks the crowded first r of correspondants, with ordinary r kept first because deletion state is not established.

The extra first-r uncertainty in correspondants was noticed within the single crop already made for its initial p. No second crop of the word was made. In the second cochaine, the old h in the next cell is a material additional correction compared with C.

The star over the first underlined O was cropped because its manufacture/hand distinction remained open after the half. The crop shows serifed typewriter-like x arms crossed by a horizontal stroke; * was retained as the composite star, without a hand-addition wrapper. This is not listed as a change because both witnesses already give the same star reading.

Differences already settled by a half have explicit half references in scan_shows and usually empty crop_ids. The main reader must make or inspect their own adjudication crops for those differences. No reader crop is being claimed where none was made.

The retained article la before champ, the ending fonctoriel after isomorphisme d'associativité, the spelling cochaine without circumflex, and the ending correspondants are not silently regularised. The displayed literal typewriter x is retained rather than normalised to a multiplication glyph.
